articles.title: Country star Jimmie Allen says he’s the ‘victim’ after $1.8M judgment in sexual assault lawsuit
articles.summary: Jimmie Allen claims he is the "victim" and reveals the dark mental health spiral that followed two sexual assault lawsuits and a default judgment.
articles.body: Jimmie Allen is maintaining his innocence and insisting he is the "victim" after a federal judge ordered the country star to pay nearly $1.8 million to a woman who accused him of sexual assault. The 41-year-old singer faced two separate civil sexual assault and abuse lawsuits from two women in 2023. During an interview with Fox News Digital, Allen spoke candidly about the allegations that derailed his career, maintaining that his sexual encounters with both women who sued him were consensual while acknowledging that he was unfaithful to his then-wife, Alexis Gale. When asked what he would say to his accusers today, Allen said he has forgiven both women but admitted that he struggled with being unable to publicly defend himself without being accused of blaming alleged victims. JIMMIE ALLEN PUBLICLY APOLOGIZES TO ESTRANGED WIFE FOR ‘HUMILIATING HER’ WITH ‘AFFAIR’ AFTER SEX ABUSE LAWSUIT "I wanted to just get on social media and call them liars and things like that," Allen said. "But it was interesting when I thought about it, someone said, 'No, well, you'll be a victim blamer and stuff like that.'" "But I was like, 'I'm the victim here,'" he continued. "So they can say this about me, these horrible things about me and try to ruin and destroy everything that I worked my butt off for. But I can't say that they're lying." In May 2023, the first woman, Jane Doe 1, who worked as the country singer's day-to-day manager, filed a lawsuit against Allen, in which she accused him of raping her in 2021 and subsequently sexually harassing her over the next 18 months. JARED LETO RESPONDS TO SEXUAL MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS MADE BY MULTIPLE WOMEN IN EXPLOSIVE DOCUMENTARY The second woman sued Allen in June 2023, accusing the "Big In A Small Town" singer of sexually assaulting her while she visited him at a Las Vegas hotel in the summer of 2022 while he was in Sin City for a bowling tournament. Jane Doe 2 claimed Allen had also recorded the encounter without her permission. Allen denied both women's allegations and filed counterclaims against them in July 2023, accusing his former manager of defamation and other claims and accusing Jane Doe 2 of unlawfully taking his cellphone following their encounter. In August 2025, Allen was found liable by default rather than following a trial in which a jury weighed the competing accounts. The following June, a federal judge ordered Allen to pay Jane Doe 2 $1,790,541 in compensatory and punitive damages. WATCH HERE: JIMMIE ALLEN SAYS HE'S THE ‘VICTIM’ AFTER SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS UPENDED HIS LIFE KATY PERRY UNDER POLICE INVESTIGATION OVER RUBY ROSE'S SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS While speaking with Fox News Digital, Allen said that he does not intend to simply accept the judgment. "I'm pursuing options because I – me as a man and as a father and as the son and brother of real sexual assault victims – I cannot in good conscience do that," he said. "And that's why I feel like as a man and as a father, it is my job to fight it and find and chase whatever other options I can." Allen did not specify what legal action he intended to pursue. Fox News Digital reached out to his current attorney, Ted Anastasiou, for comment. The default ruling followed a series of missed deadlines and court orders. According to court records, Allen and his touring company failed to meet discovery requirements, attend court-ordered mediation and obtain new counsel within deadlines set by the court. Allen claimed that much of the breakdown was due to his former attorney, Alandis Brassel, becoming seriously ill while representing him. The singer told Fox News Digital that Brassel was a solo practitioner and claimed that he had difficulty reaching his lawyer while he was sick. "I'm not in contact with the court. He is," Allen recalled. "So during that time, we missed a deadline." Allen said Brassel later informed the court about his illness but claimed the judge "didn't care." "So the judge dropped my countersuit, and they awarded Jane Doe 2 default judgment because I missed the deadline," he said. However, court records detail multiple missed deadlines and failures to comply with court orders. The Grammy Award nominee acknowledged that there was at least one deadline during that period of time that he believed he could have met himself. "I have no problem taking responsibility," Allen said. "I could have, you know, maybe done more. Absolutely." "The other ones, I should have been more, I guess, involved with the court, but I've never been in a situation like this," he continued. "I didn't know even how to connect with the court. I didn't know if I could speak to the court without my lawyer because he was the one that was handling it." Anastasiou later became Allen's legal representation. After the default ruling, Anastasiou similarly blamed Allen's "prior counsel's repeated failures to comply with discovery obligations and court orders" and said his client intended to seek to set aside the judgment. "This ruling was not based on the merits of the allegations. Mr. Allen has consistently and unequivocally maintained his innocence, and he firmly denies these accusations," Anastasiou told People magazine in August 2025. "As with earlier accusations brought on the same baseless grounds, this case is equally meritless," he continued. "The default judgment reflects the shortcomings of prior representation, not any wrongdoing by Mr. Allen. It is well-established that a client should not be penalized for the failures of their attorney, and Mr. Allen should not be deprived of his right to a fair defense." Fox News Digital was unable to reach Brassel for comment. WATCH HERE: JIMMIE ALLEN SAYS HE'S ‘PURSUING OPTIONS’ TO FIGHT $1.8M SEXUAL ASSAULT According to her lawsuit, Jane Doe 2 met Allen on a flight to Nashville in May 2022 and the two remained in contact over the following months before meeting in Las Vegas. FORMER MIT SCIENTIST WINS $6M DEFAMATION VERDICT AGAINST COLLEAGUE WHO ACCUSED HIM OF SEXUAL MISCONDUCT Jane Doe 2 alleged that she willingly joined Allen in his hotel room and initially consented to having sex with him, but repeatedly told the singer that she was not on birth control and did not want him to ejaculate inside her. According to the complaint, Allen agreed but later disregarded her requests to stop and instead ejaculated inside her. She also alleged that Allen secretly recorded their sexual encounter without her knowledge or consent. According to the lawsuit, Allen had asked her to remain on the hotel room's balcony after they arrived while he went inside, which she believed was because he was planning a surprise. Jane Doe 2 alleged that Allen instead used the opportunity to position his cellphone to later record them. Jane Doe 2 alleged that after Allen fell asleep, she discovered the phone recording them, stopped the recording and deleted the video. According to the complaint, she was unable to permanently delete the footage without Allen's passcode and took the phone with her when she left the hotel room before later turning it over to police. EX-MAYOR FOUND LIABLE FOR ALLEGED SEXUAL ASSAULTS OF 7 WOMEN, ORDERED TO PAY $13M Allen disputed Jane Doe 2's account, maintaining that their encounter was consensual and that she knew she was being recorded. He said that they were together on the balcony when he explicitly told her he wanted to record and asked permission. While speaking with Fox News Digital, he described their alleged conversation regarding the recording. "She said, ‘You were recording us without my permission.’ I said, 'Oh, no, no.' I said, 'We were on the balcony.' And I have all this in texts that we were on the balcony. I told you, 'I'm recording, is it OK?' And I don't ever hide my camera, ever. Ever. It's not my thing,'" he told Fox News Digital. Allen has maintained since 2023 that Jane Doe consented to the recording. The singer claimed to Fox News Digital that the recording depicts him "passing out." "In the video, you can see me passing out," he claimed. "You can see me black out, like pass out." Allen further claimed the recording shows Jane Doe 2 continuing to engage in sexual activity with him after he passed out, later getting dressed, returning to bed and rubbing his back before approaching the camera and turning it off. WATCH HERE: JIMMIE ALLEN SAYS SEXUAL ASSAULT LAWSUIT ‘LITERALLY SAVED MY LIFE’ AFTER DOCTOR'S DIRE WARNING Elizabeth Fegan, an attorney who represented both Jane Doe 1 and Jane Doe 2, blasted Allen's claims in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Mr. Allen's attempt to portray himself as the victim is as outrageous as it is offensive to the women who have come forward to report his sexual misconduct," Fegan said. "Two women have accused Mr. Allen of sexual abuse. Rather than accepting responsibility for his actions, he has repeatedly denied their accounts, sought to discredit them, and now attempts to rewrite the facts through the media, all while evading his financial obligations to the women who sought justice through the courts." "Let there be no ambiguity: Jane Doe 2 never consented to being recorded," she continued. "Mr. Allen's continued insistence otherwise does not change her account or the Court's findings. Nor do his self-serving descriptions of selected portions of the recording establish consent to its creation. His attempt to shift attention to her behavior is yet another effort to blame the woman whose rights he violated." JIMMIE ALLEN WELCOMES THIRD CHILD WITH ESTRANGED WIFE AMID SPLIT, SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS "The real victim here is the woman whose privacy, bodily autonomy, and trust were violated and who has endured years of trauma and litigation seeking accountability," Fegan added. "Mr. Allen has had ample opportunity to tell his story in court. He chose not to do so. He should stop attacking the women who came forward and start taking responsibility for his conduct." While speaking with Fox News Digital, Allen also addressed the allegations made by his former day-to-day manager, whose 2023 lawsuit first thrust the country singer into the scandal. Jane Doe 1, who worked as Allen's day-to-day manager, accused the singer of repeatedly sexually harassing and assaulting her over an approximately 18-month period while she was employed by his management company. In her lawsuit, Jane Doe 1 alleged that Allen first sexually assaulted her in March 2021 after a work trip to Los Angeles, where he was filming an appearance on "American Idol." She claimed that after having several drinks at a business dinner, she woke up naked in her hotel room with Allen beside her and had no memory of what happened after dinner. According to the complaint, she was bleeding and in pain and Allen insisted that she take Plan B. Jane Doe 1 alleged that Allen continued to sexually harass and assault her afterward, including by touching her without her consent and forcing her to engage in sexual acts despite her objections. She claimed she repeatedly told Allen "no," pushed him away and tried to avoid being alone with him, but feared that resisting him could jeopardize her career because she was responsible for managing him. While speaking with Fox News Digital, Allen vehemently denied Jane Doe 1's allegations but acknowledged that the two had a sexual relationship, which he characterized as a consensual affair that continued on and off for approximately a year and a half. "What I want people to understand about those allegations is one, they're not true," he claimed. "I had an affair off and on for like a year and a half with my day-to-day manager," Allen said. "And it started, then we would cut it off, and it would start, and then we will cut it off. And it slowly became one of the things where I was like, I know what I was doing was wrong, but I was afraid to end it because I didn't really know exactly how to end without one, hurting her, right, and without hurting myself. Because it's one of those things where it's like you spend so much time, go, go, go, go, go on the road. And, you know, we were around each other a lot. We were adults that made a decision." While speaking with Fox News Digital, Allen accepted responsibility for having the extramarital relationship but denied Jane Doe 1's characterization of it as sexual abuse. "If I would have never cheated on my wife, I wouldn't have been in that situation anyway," he said. "And that's the part that I take accountability for." Allen and his former manager reached a settlement in 2024 in which they agreed to dismiss their respective claims against each other. Jane Doe 1's attorney said at the time that she continued to stand by her sexual assault allegations against Allen and had agreed to settle to avoid reliving the alleged abuse at trial. While Allen maintained he never sexually assaulted either woman, he told Fox News Digital he does not consider himself blameless for the circumstances that led to the scandal. "Did I cheat on my wife? Yes. Did I apologize to my wife? Yes. Did I owe my wife an apology? Absolutely," he said. "And I'm not going to put the blame on my life on those two individuals. Yes, they might've fabricated a story, but I still slept with them and I put myself in that position." While speaking with Fox News Digital, Allen recalled the impact that the allegations had on his personal and professional life. The singer said that he would tell his accusers that they "made life really hard for my kids." Allen and Gale, who share daughters Naomi and Zara and son Cohen, initially separated and filed for divorce in April 2023, shortly before the first sexual assault lawsuit was filed against the singer. They simultaneously announced that Gale was pregnant with their third child, Cohen. In a May 2023 Instagram post, Allen apologized to Gale for having an affair and acknowledged that his choices brought shame and humiliation to his family. Gale gave birth to Cohen in September 2023 and the following month, Allen's representative said the divorce had not been completed and that the couple had decided to "work on things" and were still together. The former couple's divorce was ultimately finalized in October 2024. Allen told Fox News Digital that the "hardest conversation" that he had was with Gale. He admitted that he failed to even warn his then-wife before the first lawsuit became public. "I handled that completely wrong," Allen said. Allen said the fallout also affected his oldest son, Aadyn, whom he shares with a previous partner. He recalled struggling to explain why some of his son's friends stopped speaking to him or inviting him to parties after the allegations against his father became public. The singer also recalled how his thriving career collapsed amid the scandal and worried about how he would continue providing for his children. "Everything I've worked for is just gone," he said. "Record label gone, management gone, bookings gone, PR gone, endorsement deals gone." He said that his mounting fears sent him into an increasingly dark place and eventually led him to contemplate taking his own life. "Two years ago, I was riding around my truck at like three in the morning and I had my gun in my lap and I was trying to decide, do I want to live or not?" he told Fox News Digital. Allen said he eventually sought help, turning to therapy and spending time in rehabilitation as he worked to get his mental health back on track. He recalled that his struggles had begun well before the allegations became public. As Allen's career took off, the singer said he began taking pills to stay awake and others to keep himself in a good mood while trying to meet the demands of touring, his record label, radio, his family and fans. Allen said that by 2021 and 2022, he felt like he was on a "train" going "a thousand miles an hour," knowing he needed to get off but unsure how. "I would say in 2023, when that lawsuit came out, I felt like that was God derailing the train," he said. "One, it hurt because of what was being said about me. But at the same time, it literally saved my life." "My doctor said if I had kept going, I'd have been dead in six months," Allen continued. Allen told Fox News Digital that getting help also forced him to reconsider his relationship with music, which he admitted he had grown to hate at the height of his struggles. However, Allen said that as he worked to rebuild his life, he also began rediscovering the love of music that he had lost. Allen told Fox News Digital that while some relationships disappeared amid the controversy, he was surprised by the support he received from others in the entertainment industry. "Dolly Parton being one of them," he said. "She called me, and she told me she loves me. She said, ‘Jimmie, I know who you are.’ She said, ‘Try to just keep yourself surrounded by people that love you.’" Allen recalled Jelly Roll, Darius Rucker, Kathie Lee Gifford and Kid Rock were among others who reached out to him. Kid Rock's support eventually extended beyond words of encouragement. The "Freedom Was a Highway" singer recently collaborated with Kid Rock on his Christian album "Halfway to Jesus," marking another step in Allen's return to recording music. Allen recalled Kid Rock telling him, "'As Christians, we're quick to ask for forgiveness but don't want to give it.'" He said his approach to his career has changed dramatically from the relentless pursuit of success that he described before the allegations surfaced. "It's not about winning Grammys or CMAs or number one records," he said. "It's about doing what I love." articles.title: In 1998, Denzel Washington sponsored Chadwick Boseman’s Oxford acting programme; years later, ‘Black Panther’ star recalled his ‘you owe me money’ response
articles.summary: Long before Chadwick Boseman became a household name for playing T’Challa in Marvel’s Black Panther, a helping hand from veteran actor Denzel Washington
articles.body: Long before Chadwick Boseman became a household name for playing T’Challa in Marvel’s Black Panther, a helping hand from veteran actor Denzel Washington had quietly supported his journey towards becoming an actor. Boseman was among a group of students from Howard University who received financial assistance to attend a summer acting programme in Oxford, England. At the time, he had no idea that Washington was one of the people who had contributed towards his fees.Years later, after Boseman had established himself in Hollywood, he finally got the opportunity to thank the veteran actor in person. However, Washington’s response was far from the emotional exchange one might have expected. He greeted the future Marvel star with a playful reminder that he still owed him money, turning a meaningful moment into a memorable anecdote.How Denzel Washington helped Chadwick Boseman attend an acting programme in OxfordThe story dates back to 1998, when Boseman was studying at Howard University in Washington, D.C. He and fellow students had been accepted into a summer theatre programme at the British American Drama Academy (BADA) in Oxford. Although the opportunity offered valuable exposure to theatre and acting, the cost of attending posed a financial challenge.Their acting teacher, Phylicia Rashad, best known for her role in The Cosby Show, approached several of her celebrity friends for assistance. Washington was among those who agreed to contribute towards the students’ expenses. According to BADA, Boseman was one of ten Howard University students who attended its Midsummer in Oxford programme with support from Rashad, Washington and other donors.The contribution was made without Washington seeking public recognition for it. Boseman later learnt who had helped him when he received a letter informing him that his tuition had been paid for by Washington.Chadwick Boseman kept the story private for yearsBoseman did not immediately reveal the identity of the person who had helped fund his studies. In a 2018 appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, he explained that he had kept the information to himself for much of his career.The actor said he had received a beneficiary letter after returning from the programme, which identified Washington as the person who had paid for him. Discovering that the acclaimed Hollywood star had contributed towards his education left a lasting impression on him.Boseman also explained that he wanted to wait until he had achieved a certain level of professional success before speaking publicly about the gesture. He did not want his gratitude to be mistaken for an attempt to gain something from the established actor.Denzel Washington’s unexpected response when they finally metThe two actors eventually met in person around the time of the 2018 Academy Awards, when Boseman was enjoying the success of Black Panther. The film’s release had brought him international recognition, giving him an opportunity to acknowledge the person whose generosity had helped him years earlier.During an interview on the Oscars red carpet, Boseman recalled Washington’s reaction when he approached him. Rather than responding with a formal exchange of thanks, Washington jokingly said, “You owe me money!” He followed it with another quip: “I came to collect!”Boseman described the conversation as fun. The light-hearted response made the encounter particularly memorable, even though the original contribution had been a gesture of support rather than a conventional loan.Chadwick Boseman publicly thanked Washington at the AFI tributeBoseman later shared the story again in June 2019, when he paid tribute to Washington at the American Film Institute’s Life Achievement Award ceremony honouring the veteran actor.During his speech, Boseman recalled how Washington had agreed to help nine other theatre students from Howard University who had been accepted into the Oxford programme. He described the moment of discovering that his benefactor was someone he admired on screen as an extraordinary experience.Boseman also credited Washington’s contribution as an important part of his own journey, famously declaring, “There is no Black Panther without Denzel Washington.”His words highlighted how a relatively private act of generosity could have a lasting impact on another person’s life and career.From an aspiring actor to Marvel’s Black PantherBoseman’s career subsequently took him from stage and television work to some of Hollywood’s most prominent films. Before becoming T’Challa in Captain America: Civil War (2016) and Black Panther (2018), he portrayed several influential real-life figures, including baseball legend Jackie Robinson in 42 (2013), soul musician James Brown in Get on Up (2014) and Supreme Court Justice Thurgood Marshall in Marshall (2017).Released in 2018, Black Panther became a major cultural and commercial success, earning more than $1.3 billion worldwide. The film received seven Academy Award nominations and won three, including awards for costume design, production design and original score.Boseman’s performance as T’Challa helped establish the character as one of the Marvel Cinematic Universe’s most recognisable heroes. His journey from a student seeking opportunities to a leading Hollywood actor made the story of Washington’s early support particularly resonant.Denzel Washington and Chadwick Boseman’s connection continued beyond the scholarshipTheir connection extended beyond the Oxford programme. Washington later served as a producer on Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom (2020), one of Boseman’s final films, which also starred Viola Davis.Boseman died on August 28, 2020, at the age of 43, following a private four-year battle with colon cancer. He had continued working during his illness, delivering a widely praised performance in Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom, released posthumously later that year.Following Boseman’s death, Washington paid tribute to him, describing him as a gentle soul and a brilliant artist whose performances would endure. Their story remains a reminder of the impact that support offered early in someone’s journey can have, even when the person receiving it goes on to achieve success far beyond what either individual could have anticipated.Washington’s contribution did not make Boseman’s achievements possible on its own, but it helped him access an important educational opportunity. And years later, when the two actors finally spoke about it face-to-face, Washington’s humorous demand for repayment gave their story an unexpectedly warm ending.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Mika Singh slams Uttarakhand minister Subodh Uniyal over Daler Mehndi row and demands apology; says, 'An artist deserves dignity, regardless of the circumstances'
articles.summary: Mika Singh has asked Uttarakhand Cabinet Minister Subodh Uniyal to apologise for his remarks to Daler Mehndi during a stage show.
articles.body: Mika Singh has asked Uttarakhand Cabinet Minister Subodh Uniyal to apologise for his remarks to Daler Mehndi during a stage show. In a new post on X, Mika questioned whether the minister wants artists to stay away from the state. The minister had reprimanded the Punjabi singer mid-performance and suggested that he was intoxicated, a claim that has not been independently verified.What Mika Singh shared on XMika Singh pointed out that the minister has still not apologised for comments made on a public platform. In his caption, he wrote, “The way Minister @SubodhUniyal1 ji spoke on stage was extremely rude and disrespectful. An artist deserves dignity, regardless of the circumstances. He reportedly said on stage, “Yahan aapse pehle @manindarbuttar pit ke gaya tha. Itna pita tha ki ab uska baap bhi nahi aa sakta yahan se (Before you, someone got beaten up here and in such a way that even his father cannot come here again).”Mika added, “Is this really the language a minister should use for artists? What kind of behaviour is this? Artists come to perform, entertain people, and honour their commitments. They deserve respect, not humiliation from a public platform. Subodh Uniyal ji, do you want artists to stop coming to Uttarakhand? Such an attitude can discourage artists from performing in a state that we all love.”He also appealed to the minister directly. “Please remember that the people have given you the position you hold today. Public office comes with responsibility, humility, and accountability. I have immense love and respect for Uttarakhand, but artists deserve respect too. I sincerely hope you will reflect on your words and address this matter with dignity.”What happened at the New Tehri event?Daler Mehndi performed at the Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in New Tehri, Uttarakhand, on Sunday night. Uniyal interrupted him mid-performance and reprimanded him on stage. The minister criticised the singer’s conduct and said, “You cannot even speak, so how are you going to sing?” The remark hinted that the singer was intoxicated. The clip soon spread widely on social media.Minister explains why he spoke upLater, Subodh Uniyal told ANI why he had questioned Daler Mehndi in public. “He is a big artist. If a big artist doesn’t do justice to their art... He seemed disoriented on stage and didn’t seem to be able to even keep standing. Besides this, he was only lip-syncing to his songs. I told him that he is a big artist and he should do justice to his art; he had been offered ₹35 lakh to come and perform, but he was not even singing. So, I expressed my resentment.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! Claim your exclusive TOI Masterclass spot today!

articles.body: Pierce Brosnan is opening up about how he has prepared his sons for the acting world. The 73-year-old actor spoke with Fox News Digital at the premiere of his son Paris' new film, "Seniors," about Paris' acting career and how he's warned his sons about how "tough" the entertainment industry is. "No, it's a very tough business, it is a very capricious business at times, but Paris has the strength and the stamina, he has a talent there, he's got a charisma, and he's got good sense and intuition, he really has a talent there that will need to be nurtured and worked on," he said. "The work that you need to do, the discipline it takes to be an actor, to work on your voice, to work on your body, to work on your mind and the discipline of reading and studying. So he has all of that." The "Die Another Day" star shares two sons with his wife, Keely Shaye Smith — Dylan, 29, and Paris, 25 — and welcomed Sean, 43, with his late first wife, Cassandra Harris. He also adopted Harris' two children from a previous relationship, Christopher, 53, and Charlotte, who died in 2013 at the age of 41. articles.title: New movies to watch this weekend: See 'Clayface' and 'Wicker' in theaters, rent or buy 'The Weight,' stream 'The Invite' on HBO Max
articles.summary: Our critic takes on the week's big movie releases, from the chilling comic book film 'Clayface" to Jenna Ortega's "Klara and the Sun."
articles.body:
Welcome to Trust Me, I Watch Everything , a weekly guide to notable new movies opening or becoming available each Friday.

Leading theaters this week are the latest DC comic book movie Clayface and the sexy fable Wicker, which had a steamy trailer that went viral earlier this year.

If you'd prefer a movie night at home, you can rent or buy the killer low-budget thriller The Weight with Ethan Hawke and Russell Crowe, or check out Mark Wahlberg's By Any Means.

And over on streaming services you're likely already paying for, The Cycle, a new horror movie worth your time, debuts on Shudder. Plus, one of the year's best comedies, The Invite, finally makes it way to HBO Max.

Why I liked it: The DC Universe now appears to be taking cues from those "Spider-Man villain origin stories that do not in any way feature Spider-Man for contractual reasons" like Venom, Morbius and Madame Web. Clayface shows us the birth of an antihero who roams the streets of Gotham and will presumably encounter Batman in the future at some point, offscreen.

Thankfully for James Gunn and Peter Safran — the latest architects of Warner Bros.' DCU, which is off to a rough-ish start after this summer's Supergirl — Clayface is far more satisfying. It plays more like a Universal Monster movie or something akin to Sam Raimi's cult classic Darkman. It's also borrowing heavily from stuff like The Fly and The Thing, as well as from more obscure genre fare like Basket Case and the works of Brian Yuzna.

Matt Hagen's (Tom Rhys Harries) meteoric rise from Gotham street kid to Hollywood leading man is tragically cut short when a local crime boss's actions leave him horribly disfigured. Abandoned by his team and left with nothing, Matt seeks out a cutting-edge treatment that miraculously returns him to his former self but also unexpectedly affects his grip on reality, sending him spiraling down a destructive path of all-consuming revenge.

What the movie lacks in a compelling screenplay it more than makes up for with nasty gore that will make you wince, from the initial face-slashing to the wild ways in which Matt's face contorts and distorts itself after he injects himself with nanocells. It also sports some very ugly fake digital background work — is it really that hard to just film in an area that has an actual train? — but that's hardly movie-ruining.

The movie is at its most effective when it's showcasing its extremely hard-R-rated body horror, which thankfully manifests itself in various incredibly effective ways throughout. At one point he's forced to do some light facial surgery during extreme turbulence on an airplane, like a particularly evil Jackass segment.

Clayface may be little more than a pastiche of more successful fare, but it gets enough right to recommend for fans of squirm-inducing body horror. DC should be begging in-demand filmmaker of the moment Zach Cregger to come over to Warner Bros. and make his passion-project spec script Henchman , though I fear that unless Clayface is a big hit, it might be a tough sell.

What other critics are saying : Reviews are mixed but lean positive. The AP's Mark Kennedy writes, "We may not have asked for it, but it's a crowd-pleaser, mimicking its title character's ability to be a little something for everyone." David Fear at Rolling Stone , however, calls it "the equivalent of eating a handful of Play-Doh™, and twice as flavorless."

How to watch: Clayface is now playing in theaters nationwide .

This review was written by my colleague Kelsey Weekman .

Why it's worth seeing: Since its ovation-earning premiere at the Sundance Film Festival in January, I have been unable to avoid advertising for the steamy basket movie, Wicker. I know that, as a millennial woman who loves yearning and wants filmmakers to stop toning down their sex scenes , I am the film's exact target audience.

Part Bridgerton and part dark fairy tale, it's about an enigmatic middle-aged fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) who asks a basket weaver (Peter Dinklage) to make her a husband out of wicker. She's not too concerned with the pageantry of marriage in her small medieval farming town, where all men are known by their profession and women are known by their husbands, but she harbors a secret, worldly desire for something more. The basket weaver obliges, and she marries Alexander Skarsgård's basket man, complete with woven muscles and real human eyes, whose work around the house and constant satiation of her carnal desires make all the townsfolk jealous.

The moan-filled trailer went viral in July, inspiring people ( and brands ) to unite in their thirst for a nice basket guy and muse about what women truly want from their relationships. It's turned the movie into a cultural phenomenon. You can take photos with a Wicker cutout and see the movie in a multisensory 4DX screening .

It's hard for anything to live up to so much hype, but I'm thrilled to say that the movie, in my opinion, accomplished exactly what it set out to do. There's a lot of pleasure, both physical and emotional, as Skarsgård's basket man repeatedly breaks the bed — and repeatedly fixes it — while saying things like, "I was made to be with you."

The portrayal of this patriarchal society is a bit on the nose at times: Women gleefully lock their necks in a collar during their wedding ceremonies, and they're all vengefully jealous of this wicker guy who actually does housework, and so on. Sometimes it feels like the movie is aggressively pointing out aspects of modern life that still feel antiquated and oppressive, but sometimes you really do just want a man to set societal expectations aside, fix a leaky roof and make you feel good, just for the love of the game.

The wicker man isn't just a hunk who does chores. He absolutely adores the fisherwoman. In one scene, she confesses she doesn't know how to dance as the couples around them do complicated but goofy routines in the town square. But he lovingly and gently holds her as they sway, making everyone else seethe with envy. I was genuinely struck by the sentimental bangers the wicker man whispers to the fisherwoman, like, "Without you … I would never have seen the sun on the ocean or the clouds in the sky."

Make no mistake, there's a lot of sex in this movie, which stands out in a time when so many movies and TV shows cut sex scenes to avoid spooking prudish audiences. But this film has very little nudity, which makes it feel less about the look of sex than the feeling of it. It's about desire, not objectification. I loved that.

The initial clichés of the premise that reeled me in were all subverted by the end, thanks in part to clever writing, but also to the acting masterclass put on by Colman (an Oscar-winning acting heavyweight turned indie darling) and Skarsgård (one of the hottest weird little freak actors in human history). I'll defend heartwarming straight-to-streaming slop any day — there just isn't enough to keep up with demand! — but Wicker feels so original and clever that it earns any of its mushiness, as well as your ticket money. And it's hot.

What other critics are saying: They're enamored! Richard Lawson at the Hollywood Reporter calls it "a warming, sometimes poignant pleasure, a film full of lively personality and possessed of a rather humane outlook on our petty foibles. It is not exactly forgiving, though; the movie has a harder, more merciless edge than one might expect." Amy Nicholson of the Los Angeles Times found it "funny and sexy" but found fault with the film's second half: "The fisherwoman's love story is Wicker 's pulse, but the movie is really about the town, and it sidelines her character to skewer the place."

How to watch: Wicker is now playing in theaters nationwide .

Klara and the Sun : Taika Waititi may not have been the best person to adapt this acclaimed Kazuo Ishiguro book, as his signature quirky humor rarely works as intended here. Jenna Ortega stars as Klara, an "Artificial Friend" who finds a deep bond with a troubled young girl, bringing light and hope to a grieving family through her unwavering devotion and innocent wonder. It's treading familiar ground — Steven Spielberg's AI: Artificial Intelligence just turned 25 — and despite Ortega's best efforts and a very game physical performance, the movie becomes a saccharine grab bag of tearjerker clichés. The melancholy material deserved more earnest treatment than Waititi gives it, and every attempt at a joke repeatedly falls flat. But Ortega really is great as Klara, expressive and childlike and full of wonder at the most basic concepts. Get tickets .

Wildwood : The beloved animation house Laika Studios returns with its most ambitious project yet, a stop-motion film that spent 16 years in development and was painstakingly handcrafted every step of the way. In the fantasy epic based on the book of the same name, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel launches a desperate rescue mission after her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, leading her into an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Ore. Joined by a hapless but loyal classmate, Prue risks it all as she navigates a world of bandits, talking animals and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. I can't wait to catch up with it; critics can't stop raving about it . Get tickets .

Ali G: Who Iz I? : The latest comedy from provocateur and comedian Sacha Baron Cohen follows in his tradition of character-based antics and pranks on unsuspecting strangers (see: Borat , Bruno and his previous Ali G film). After 20 years of chilling, Ali G is shocked to learn that his girlfriend is eight months pregnant. Faced with an extra mouth to feed, he heads to America to reclaim his former glory, but soon encounters adversaries who threaten his very existence. Get tickets .

Why I liked it: The 1950 novel The Wages of Fear by Georges Arnaud , already made in France in 1953, was famously adapted by William Friedkin in 1977 as Sorcerer , which, just as famously, bombed miserably at the box office due to its opening on the heels of a little-known sci-fi flick called Star Wars.

Sorcerer is an incredible movie that has, thankfully, become a cult classic. After decades of being hard to find, it's recently been restored in 4K and regularly plays at repertory cinemas. Friedkin considered it to be his finest work.

All of which is to say that The Weight is a Depression-era survival thriller heist western that feels heavily inspired by Sorcerer, but made on a minuscule budget and under far less strenuous circumstances. It's tense, well-acted and a worthy take on the doomed men-on-a-mission movie.

When Samuel (Ethan Hawke) is torn from his daughter and sent to a brutal prison, Warden Clancy (Russell Crowe) offers him a high-stakes proposition: smuggle gold out of a remote mine with a dangerous crew of prisoners, and he'll win his freedom.

It's stripped-down as can be, but that doesn't stop it from being incredibly tense, with a particularly memorable scene unfolding on a sketchy drawbridge in what appears to be a direct nod to Sorcerer, albeit under very different circumstances. The Weight manages to convey its huge stakes despite its humble budget. It's one of the best movies of the year that you likely haven't heard of.

What other critics are saying: Reviews are very strong. The AP's Lindsay Bahr writes, "It is very much a 'dad movie,' which isn't, in this case, a bad or even limiting thing. More than a few people have compared it to something Clint Eastwood might have done at some point — just a solid, hearty, meat-and-potatoes kind of movie." David Fear at Rolling Stone says it's "not a perfect homage to 1970s tough-guy action flicks. But The Weight is close enough to give you that same thrill you get when, say, an old-timey James Coburn or Lee Marvin movie unexpectedly shows up on TCM."

How to watch: The Weight is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV , Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

Why you should skip it: Mark Wahlberg gets top billing, but his prosthetic nose and toothpick do most of the heavy lifting in By Any Means, a '60s-set movie that can best be described as " Green Book but with mob violence."

A young Black FBI agent (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II) is sent to Mississippi to investigate a wave of brutal killings targeting civil rights leaders. Forced to work alongside notorious mafia hitman Greg Scarpa (Wahlberg), he finds himself pulled into a deadly hunt where justice and vengeance begin to blur.

It's based on a true story, but Wahlberg's turn as Scarpa is more a caricature of a Brooklyn mobster than a thoughtful portrayal of an interesting character. It's no Mississippi Burning.

What other critics are saying : The reviews are not kind. The AV Club's Monica Castillo writes, "[Director Elegance] Bratton uses the film to prove he has the big-budget chops to handle movie stars, and Abdul-Mateen plays out each of his character's conflicted feelings with nuance, but they're both overshadowed by the antics of Wahlberg's dead-eyed antihero." Owen Myers at the Guardian , however, dug it well enough, writing, "The result is grimly effective while also being one of the most grisly and upsetting films in recent memory. As a provocation, By All Means is hard to forget."

How to watch: By Any Means is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV , Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom : Fans of Aardman Animations are in for a treat with this one, the third Shaun the Sheep movie, which is a spinoff of Wallace and Gromit. On Halloween Eve at Mossy Bottom Farm, excitement turns to dismay when the clumsy Farmer ruins the pumpkin patch. Shaun tries fixing it with science experiments, but things go wrong when a wild beast appears in the woods. The joy here lies in discovering how the filmmakers craft a dialogue-free movie that entertains kids and adults alike, with plenty of sight gags and other clever bits. Rent or buy .

📺 Movies newly available on streaming services you may already have

Why I liked it: I don't know why I expected this to be one very specific type of horror movie, but I was particularly thrilled when it turned into a very different specific type of horror movie. The less said about it, the better, so I'll keep things short.

Centered on a daughter who unravels her father's dark past after his body, missing for 36 years, is found at a horrific crime scene, the film stars Deborah Ann Woll of True Blood fame and Burn Notice' s Jeffrey Donovan. It plays like a feature-length episode of The X-Files, a procedural that eventually leads to something particularly spooky.

Without spoiling the monstrous goods, I'll just say that the practical effects in the back half are truly spectacular — some of the best I've seen in ages — from the design to the execution. The Cycle also finds a new way into a classic horror trope that I found clever and exciting.

The Cycle is hard to talk about because all I want to do is praise the exact reasons this take on this material works so well. Just watch it, because if " X-Files Cinema" is enough of a sell for you, it will deliver.

What other critics are saying : They mostly dig it! Amelia Emberwing at Fangoria writes, " The Cycle is one of the most competent creature features we've seen in a long time. It's also scrappy, which is icing on the cake, but those accolades don't come with the 'for its budget' asterisk." The Guardian's Leslie Felperin , however, says, "It's a shame that the hardcore creature-feature stuff is a letdown because the drama leading up to it isn't bad."

How to watch: The Cycle is now streaming on Shudder and AMC+ .

Why I liked it: Olivia Wilde's third film as a director is easily her best, a laugh-out-loud funny comedy about marriage, sex, complacency and rekindling that spark. The script from Rashida Jones and Will McCormack is smart, humorous and honest; they're working from a template, though, as the movie is a remake of the 2020 Spanish film The People Upstairs, which has proven fertile ground.

This American version is one of several adaptations, with Russia, South Korea and Italy among the nations that took it for a spin. In the film, Joe and Angela's (Seth Rogen and Olivia Wilde) marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors (Edward Norton and Penélope Cruz) for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. It's a perfectly cast film that features some of the best work from all parties involved, though it's particularly nice to see Norton in a role like this, earning tons of laughs. Wilde is exceptional here too, both in front of and behind the camera.

The Invite is a movie about intimacy in marriage and how we all want to be seen and desired, even when we struggle to communicate it. But more importantly than that, it's very, very funny, and builds to an incredibly rewarding crescendo about midway through. It ends on a sweet note, making the whole experience feel more than worthwhile.

What other critics are saying: It's one of the best-reviewed films of the year. IndieWire's Kate Erbland dubs it "a truly adult comedy with plenty to say and even more laughs to share." David Fear at Rolling Stone writes, "Whether this is the beginning of the hyphenate finding a distinctive voice as a director — a Wilde style — is TBD. What's certain is that she turned a modern comedy of manners into a minor miracle."

How to watch: The Invite is now streaming on HBO Max .

One Spoon of Chocolate : This revenge thriller directed by Wu-Tang Clan's RZA is ultimately too broad in its social commentary, but it does deliver some satisfying action by the end. In the film, an ex-convict (Shameik Moore) decides to fight back when he becomes the target of a local gang and the police. It's so cartoonishly over-the-top with its racist archetype characters that it's hard to buy into, but the catharsis of watching them meet their demise does hit. Now streaming on Hulu .

Moana : The 2016 Moana is the best Disney film of the modern era. The 2026 Moana is such an embarrassment that the best we can hope for is that it bombs miserably enough that Disney is forced to go back to the drawing board — literally — and maybe try doing something original by hand again rather than crudely tracing over something it has already done. Check out my full review . Now streaming on Disney+ .

articles.title: Un restaurante tendrá que indemnizar con 4.792 euros a una camarera por despedirla tras contar chistes subidos de tono
articles.standfirst: También cabe la opción de readmitirla, abonando los salarios de tramitación
articles.summary: También cabe la opción de readmitirla, abonando los salarios de tramitación
articles.body: Un establecimiento de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria decidió despedir a una trabajadora por sus comportamientos. Desde su punto de vista, tenían motivos suficientes para ello. De hecho, se han hecho públicas algunas de sus conductas: contar chistes subidos de todo o invitar a los comensales a irse porque tenía un examen. Todo ello, después de haber estado en una baja médica durante un año. Desde el restaurante decidieron que no podían seguir así. Además, han presentado algunas quejas que dejaban los clientes en este negocio. “Finalizando el servicio, contó una anécdota personal que consideramos inapropiado: '¿A ti por qué te llaman Cerilla? Porque cada vez tengo el agujero más grande”, cuenta uno de los clientes. Otro comensal revela que vivió una “situación bastante incómoda en el restaurante debido al exceso de confianza por parte de una camarera en intervino en varias conversaciones, que mantenía con clientes los cuales se sintieron cohibidos debido a sus comentarios y chistes fuera de lugar”. Aun así, con estas pruebas, el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Canarias ha decidido revocar esta decisión. La camarera deberá ser indemnizada con 4.792 euros o, en su defecto, volver a ser contratada, abonándole los salarios de tramitación. La Justicia da por probados los hechos, pero considera que el despido es improcedente. Para llegar a esta conclusión se basa en que estas conductas no son suficientes para un despido, y sí para un reproche. Además, este juzgado deja claro que “tener cierta confianza con los clientes es algo habitual en un restaurante esté o no permitido por la empresa y forma parte de nuestras costumbres civiles”. Una decisión final que ha generado un gran revuelo en redes sociales.

articles.title: Luis Zahera, actor: "Nací en la dictadura y viendo en lo que se está convirtiendo todo, hay que posicionarse. Es momento de basta ya y no callar más"
articles.standfirst: El ganador de dos premios Goya se pronuncia en Europa Press sobre la situación actual en España
articles.summary: El ganador de dos premios Goya se pronuncia en Europa Press sobre la situación actual en España
articles.body: Luis Zahera se ha convertido en uno de los actores más respetados del panorama nacional, especialmente, por lo que ocurre delante de las cámaras. Pero detrás, el intérprete nunca ha rehuido ninguna cuestión. A raíz de su último estreno en Netflix, ‘Colisión’, ambientada en plena crisis económica en España, Zahera habla sobre la situación actual del país en Europa Press. Preguntado sobre si la trama de esta película puede resultar familiar a los espectadores actuales, el actor lo tiene claro. “Es como si la historia se repitiera”, asegura. De hecho, cree que el debate que se plantea en el filme está muy relacionado con lo que se está viviendo hoy en día: “Volvemos a caer en las garras de esos buitres, en las garras del sistema”. En el horizonte ya asoman unas elecciones en las que tampoco los actores son ajenos. El 29N ellos también irán a votar. Luis Zahera no tiene ningún temor a posicionarse y utilizar su altavoz para quien quiera escucharlo. “Soy un poco temeroso y me centro en entretener, pero los actores tenemos la responsabilidad moral de usar nuestro altavoz”, zanja sobre este asunto. “El momento es tan angustioso... Yo, que ya tengo 60 años, que nací en la dictadura y viendo en lo que se está convirtiendo todo, sí creo que hay que posicionarse”, indica el gallego sobre su forma de entender los problemas que suelen afectar al resto de la población. El ganador de dos premios Goya, por ‘As bestas’ y ‘El reino’, se muestra contundente a la hora de describir lo que está viviendo España en la actualidad: “Creo que es un momento de 'Basta ya', de movilizarnos, de, por lo menos, ser un altavoz de lo que ocurre, no callar más”.

articles.title: Yellowstone creator Taylor Sheridan brings his Texas ranch brand to Las Vegas with new steakhouse
articles.summary: The MGM Grand announced a Four Sixes Ranch Steakhouse opening in 2027, featuring Texas cuisine and custom footage from Taylor Sheridan's ranch.
articles.body: Taylor Sheridan's empire continues to grow. Sheridan is known for being the visionary responsible for the "Yellowstone" universe. The Paramount Network series starring Kevin Costner dominated TV for five seasons, and resulted in multiple prequels and spinoffs. However, Sheridan's success isn't drilled down to just the neo-Western drama. His other monster hits include "Sicario," "Wind River," "Lioness," "Landman" and several other projects. 'YELLOWSTONE' CREATOR TAYLOR SHERIDAN WAS 'HOMELESS TWICE' BEFORE BUILDING TV EMPIRE He's also the owner of the 6666 ranch in Texas, and is now linking it up with Sin City. Taylor Sheridan expands footprint in Las Vegas. There aren't many things on this planet I enjoy more than visiting Las Vegas and watching Sheridan's work. Well, the two worlds are now smashing together. The MGM Grand in Las Vegas announced on Thursday that it's opening the Four Sixes Ranch Steakhouse at the resort in 2027. The restaurant will feature "signature cuts sourced directly from Four Sixes Ranch and bold flavors rooted in authentic Texas cuisine," according to the release. Sheridan's 6666 ranch is roughly 260,000 acres and raises Angus cattle. The release also states that the restaurant will have "digital walls showcasing custom footage from Sheridan, bringing the landscapes and spirit of the American West." Sounds like the people rolling it out know the exact kind of customer they're looking to attract. This also isn't Sheridan's first rodeo (no pun intended) in Las Vegas. He previously had a popup restaurant at the Wynn in Las Vegas. More than anything, this move by Sheridan goes to show how his influence far expands past just entertainment. articles.title: Rebecca Gayheart watched Eric Dane fight for time with daughters during ‘heartbreaking’ final months
articles.summary: Rebecca Gayheart reveals the devastating moment she learned Eric Dane had ALS and how their two daughters navigated his final months together.
articles.body: As Eric Dane faced the final moments of his life, his family fought to hold on to every precious moment. Rebecca Gayheart, who remained close to Dane after they separated in 2018, opened up about his final months battling amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), the toll it took on their two daughters and how she's keeping his memory alive. Dane died Feb. 19, less than a year after publicly revealing his ALS diagnosis. "We tried to be present through all of our fear and frustration and uncertainty," Gayheart told People of the family's last months together. "It was truly an exhausting and heartbreaking experience, but it also showed us his extraordinary strength every day, and that was really wonderful for the girls and myself to witness." SANDRA BULLOCK SAYS BRYAN RANDALL WAS ILL FOR 'HALF OF OUR RELATIONSHIP' AS SHE OPENS UP ABOUT HIS DEATH While Gayheart tried to remain strong for Dane as they searched for answers about his worsening symptoms ahead of his diagnosis, she admitted nothing could have prepared her for the news that he had ALS. "I went into my closet and closed the door," she told the outlet. "I was always telling him, ‘You’re going to be okay, we’re going to figure this out.’ But that day was like a punch in the gut. It took my breath away." As Gayheart and Dane struggled to come to terms with the diagnosis themselves, they faced another challenge: explaining the news to their two young daughters. "They had so many questions, it still felt like it wasn’t real," she said. "And their father let them know that he wanted to try to spend as much time as possible with them." "I’m eating sushi with my kids, and suddenly I can’t work the chopsticks with my right hand," he wrote in his memoir, according to People. "My hand tingles, and then my fingers feel numb. Some kind of weird nerve thing, I think. I shake it off. I’m probably texting too much. Three weeks later, it happens again, only worse. I can’t grip the chopsticks at all." The emotional impact of Dane's diagnosis was something the actor also addressed in his own words. "[Rebecca and I] were married for 14 years, grew apart, filed for divorce, but never got around to signing the papers. We’ve since stayed close, co-parenting, going on vacations as a family, spending time together, and now we talk every day," Dane wrote. "I say to Rebecca on the phone, ‘It’s what we feared.’" LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "I don’t remember a single word I said after that," he recalled. "After the kids downloaded me on their day, I’d call him and be like, ‘Oh my God, there’s a boy that likes Georgia.’ Or when Billie got her driver’s license, I wanted to call him so badly because that was something he was really excited about," she told People.
